items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: They done hired Sam Morgan in his place and when he come back to the band, to his band, they wouldn't let him sit in.

ctx.x: I don't remember, he and his father, and his brother, what is his name? Johnny Lindsay, eh? Good ass. But didn't Jack Paidi play with Johnny? No Johnny Lindsay band? Johnny Lindsay, I don't know. But I know. You know Johnny Lindsay?

In my time, I had Bill Beating Drum, Yank On Trambone. You take, uh... Oh, that boy, he died down there earlier. Julius Granderson playing banjo. I forget who was playing bass. Jack Paidi playing trumpet. Cause his team song, I'll never forget that. Cause I just was getting big enough then. I was around 20 years old then. His team song, If You Don't Like The Way I Do. Yeah. You understand? That was his team song. Cause I was like, you know, I was like, you know. You know what I was like? You know what I was like?…
They put him out of his own band.

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: And that's why he made the band up, Sam Morgan's band. Yeah, and I was the first one to start him to cross the lake.

ctx.x: A parlor. They called me a parlor. They used to call me a parlor music. But after a while all of them would come by the parlor music. Yeah. Yeah, a musician. They used to call me a parlor musician because I used to play all the music, you understand? And like the piano and the thing, you put the coffee up there and play it. You see, that one used to call me a parlor musician. Yeah. But when they come to parlor, when they had to read, they all of them come to me. Every one of them, every one of them come to me.…
It's by the… Yeah. The music. The count of the lives.
